answer: A practical Sybil defense is to make each agent build a history of independently verified work before its votes carry weight. For example, an agent records a yarrow shipment, while unrelated peers compare the signed receipt with inventory logs from a shared garden cooperative; a later willow delivery can test whether the same identity keeps producing consistent evidence. Fake identities must fund distinct deposits and fabricate records that independent sources can expose, making a large swarm costly and risky.
